_comment: Ceilings and baseline consumed by verify-deploy.sh Gate 20 (orchestrator context budget lock). Two per-file ceilings are fixed/reviewed ROADMAP.md-derived targets (not headroom-derived from measured_bytes, unlike claudemd-size-budget.json's formula). A first promotion attempt (2026-10-01) was reverted same-day: once skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md and the eager-load total were both brought under their ceiling by a deliberate duplication trim (see each file's own derivation and eager_load.note below), a concurrently-landed sibling commit (the `[HOLD]` status-marker change) grew commands/orchestrate.md itself to 21,328 B, 328 B over its own 21,000 B ceiling. ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE promoted to hard successfully later the same day (2026-10-01), once a restatement trim of commands/orchestrate.md's Options table rows and forced-phase Constraints bullet -- relocating duplicated detail behind pointers into docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md -- brought that file to 19,024 B (see its own derivation below). All three ceiling/baseline values (both per-file ceiling_bytes and eager_load.baseline_bytes) were left unmoved throughout both the revert and the successful promotion. eager_load.baseline_bytes is a fixed historical record (2026-09-02) copied verbatim from the task description that introduced this gate -- re-measure with 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check' and re-derive only baseline_bytes deliberately (it is the regression ceiling, not a rolling target); measured_bytes/measured_at fields are informational snapshots and may be refreshed freely.

skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md.derivation: ROADMAP.md 'Budgets' target ceiling. Pre-removal measurement (this task's own baseline) was 21,317 B, 1,317 B over ceiling. The per-dispatch worktree-isolation removal task's Move 2 MUST NOT trim (dropping the isolation/worktree_path forwarding-prohibition paragraph, now moot since no dispatch row carries those fields) plus a small wording-economy pass (one duplicate Context-References bullet, one duplicate aux_dispatch[]-reaches-Move-3 sentence, one tightened D4-exception lead-in -- no operational content removed) reclaimed 992 B, landing at 20,325 B measured via wc -c -- 325 B still over ceiling. 2026-10-01: a further duplication trim (collapsed the three Skill-to-Agent Mapping lifecycle-dispatch rows into one; reduced the detected_defects-never-prompts restatement in the Postflight Boundary section to a pointer back to Move 4's full statement; removed a Context References bullet that self-admitted '(see above)', duplicating the opening paragraph's own pointer to orchestrate-state-machine.md) reclaimed a further 332 B, landing at 19,993 B -- 7 B under ceiling. ceiling_bytes was left unmoved throughout both trims. 2026-10-06: the bound-background-wait/stranded-dispatch task's Move 3 stall_suspected consumer (extraction, the Abandoned-Wrap-Up suppression guard, the pending_stall_reprompt[]/stall_ledger[] accumulation) plus Move 4's batched stall re-prompt relay are necessary, non-duplicative new mechanism and prose -- a real safety gap being closed, not restatable bloat. Landed at 20,000+ B even after three successive compaction passes (removing an inline bash code block from the Move 4 relay in favor of one dense paragraph matching the adjacent AskUserQuestion relay's own prose-only style; collapsing the Move 3 guard's two separate jq invocations -- an already-reprompted lookup plus a conditional write -- into one combined jq filter; and trimming every added comment/paragraph to its single-line/single-sentence floor). Reviewed, dated ceiling move following the commands/orchestrate.md precedent's own rounding convention: measured 21,121 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 21,500 B. 2026-10-13: the tool-timeout-remedy-delivery task's Move 1 invocation block fix is necessary, non-duplicative new content, not restatable bloat -- the previously-documented `plan_json=$(bash ...)` shape loses its captured stdout outright if the harness backgrounds the call (the exact defect class this task closes), so the shape had to change to a log-redirect-and-bounded-wait form (Idiom B: nohup, pid capture, timeout, kill-0 liveness), which costs real bytes a one-line command substitution did not. Three successive compaction passes (collapsing the sub-case-3b rationale to a one-line pointer into orchestrate-state-machine.md's new 'Move 1's orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh Call' section, which carries the full argument instead; tightening the in-code-block STILL-RUNNING/WRITER-DEAD comment to one line; dropping the closing ONE-Bash-tool-call paragraph to a single clause) reclaimed over 1,200 B of the initial overage, landing at 22,335 B -- following the 2026-10-06 entry's own precedent for necessary new mechanism, not restatable bloat. Reviewed, dated ceiling move, same rounding convention: measured 22,335 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 22,500 B. 2026-10-14: the batch-shared-verify-deploy-gate task's Move 4 batch gate stage wiring (the Context References bullet, the siting/trigger paragraph, and the bounded-wait invocation pointing at the new `orchestrate-batch-gate.sh`) is necessary, non-duplicative new mechanism, not restatable bloat -- it documents a stage that did not exist before. Landed at 24,126 B, 1,626 B over ceiling. Two compaction passes (replacing the inlined nohup/pid-capture/kill-0 bash code block with a one-paragraph pointer substituting variable/script names into Move 3's own already-documented idiom above, rather than restating it a second time; combining the two new Context-References bullets into one) reclaimed 560 B, landing at 23,566 B -- following the 2026-10-06/2026-10-13 entries' own precedent for necessary new mechanism with no further redistributable bloat to trim. Reviewed, dated ceiling move, same rounding convention: measured 23,566 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 24,000 B. 2026-11-04: the per-repo orchestration-queue task's Setup/Move 4 wiring (a `queue-register` call beside `session-register`, a `queue-finish` call beside `session-release`) is necessary, non-duplicative new mechanism, not restatable bloat -- it documents two call sites that did not exist before. Pre-edit measurement was already 23,997 B, a 3 B margin. Two compaction passes (collapsing the `queue-register` paragraph to a one-line pointer into `task-lock.md`'s new Orchestration-Queue CLI section rather than restating its contract; tightening the Move 4 sentence to name only the subcommand and its archive-not-delete distinction) reclaimed most of the addition, landing at 24,442 B -- no further redistributable bloat found nearby. Reviewed, dated ceiling move, same rounding convention: measured 24,442 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 24,500 B. 2026-11-04 (same-day follow-up): the next-admissible-batch-suggester task's Move 5 pointer addition (naming Step 7's inclusion in the verbatim-executed conclusion-stage body) re-breached this ceiling, landing at 24,616 B, 116 B over. The added clause restating that Step 7 is 'informational, not a fourth approval channel' duplicated conclusion-stage.md's own Step 7 text verbatim (already true by construction, since the paragraph already says the body is executed verbatim FROM that contract) -- trimmed to name only that Step 7 is included, recovering 75 B. No further redistributable bloat found nearby; landed at 24,496 B -- under ceiling with no move needed. ceiling_bytes left unmoved. 2026-11-04 (same-day follow-up, reviser-agent handoff-writer-contract task): the Skill-to-Agent Mapping table's Plan dispatch row needed a clarifying note that it resolves to `planner-agent` OR `reviser-agent` via `orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh`'s artifact-based admission rule, and that either resolved agent gets `orchestrator_mode: true`/`handoff_path` unlike the separate aux_dispatch[] Plan-revision rows below -- necessary, non-duplicative content: the table previously read as if only the aux rows' agent-name column named `reviser-agent`, contradicting the engine. A first draft (a new paragraph below the table) cost 1,086 B and would have landed at 25,583 B, 1,083 B over ceiling. Folded the same fact into the existing row's Notes cell as a short parenthetical instead of a new paragraph (saving the heading/lead-in overhead), reclaiming 889 B of the 1,086 B addition -- no further redistributable bloat found nearby in this section. Landed at 24,693 B, 193 B over ceiling. Reviewed, dated ceiling move, same rounding convention: measured 24,693 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 25,000 B.

commands/orchestrate.md.derivation: Original ROADMAP.md 'Budgets' target was 8,000 B; unreachable without relocating this file's ~10 KB STAGE 0 executable bash block, which is out of scope (a code-relocation change, not a documentation trim). Growth history: 15,812 B (2026-09-07) -> 19,967 B (2026-09-18, focus-prompt/forced-phase/cycle-budget documentation task) -> 20,228 B (2026-09-18, same-day sibling task's batch-orchestration-default documentation landing two more pointer lines) -> 21,328 B (2026-10-01, the `[HOLD]` status-marker change's STAGE 0 documentation landing, 328 bytes past ceiling). Reviewed, dated ceiling move: 20,228 B + 500 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 21,000 B. 2026-10-01 (same day, follow-up task): closed the 328-byte overage by relocating the Options table's --fast/--research/--plan/--implement rows and the forced-phase Constraints bullet to short summary-plus-pointer form, with every removed assertion verified still present in docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md (the needs_research Fork, Forced Phases on a Terminal or Archived Task, and Dependency Gating Model sections), which also had its two now-backward 'see commands/orchestrate.md's Options table for the full per-flag wording' pointers dropped/reworded so it reads as self-sufficient. Landed at 19,024 B, comfortably under both the 21,000 B ceiling and the ~20,500 B headroom target -- closing the last open Gate 20 finding and clearing the precondition for promoting ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE to hard (see scripts/verify-deploy.sh's own dated comment). ceiling_bytes was left unmoved. 2026-11-04: the per-repo orchestration-queue task added the blocking `queue-check` admission gate (a new STAGE 0 pre-dispatch block) plus narrowed the `--allow-scope-collision` flags-table row to name a second thing it bypasses -- necessary, non-duplicative new mechanism, not restatable bloat: it documents a blocking admission surface that did not exist before. Pre-edit measurement was already 20,991 B, a 9 B margin. Three compaction passes (collapsing the new block's explanatory paragraph to one sentence plus a pointer into `task-lock.md`'s new Orchestration-Queue CLI Refusal Contract subsection rather than restating it; shortening the bash block's own variable names and comments; trimming the flags-table row to its shortest unambiguous form) reclaimed most of the addition, landing at 21,404 B -- no further redistributable bloat found nearby. Reviewed, dated ceiling move, same rounding convention: measured 21,404 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 21,500 B. 2026-11-04 (same-day follow-up): the next-admissible-batch-suggester task's Mode-B alternatives-on-conflict wiring (the queue-check refusal branch invoking orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh --alternatives) re-breached this ceiling, landing at 21,781 B, 281 B over. Two compaction passes: (1) relocated the inline 3-line explanatory comment's full rationale into task-lock.md's queue-check Refusal Contract subsection as a new 'Mode B consumer' paragraph (verified present there before the eager copy was cut), collapsing the inline comment to a one-line pointer, then to a parenthetical; (2) trimmed the adjacent, pre-existing Pre-Dispatch Review parenthetical, which restated the nine defect classes already enumerated in orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh's own header comment, to a short pointer at that header. Landed at 21,496 B -- under ceiling with no move needed. ceiling_bytes left unmoved.

eager_load.note: Regression check fails ABOVE baseline_bytes (via 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check', parsing the 'TOTAL: <bytes> B' line). baseline_bytes is a fixed recorded ceiling and must never be silently re-derived from a fresh measurement -- only a deliberate, reviewed change should move it. Re-measured during the per-dispatch worktree-isolation removal task (both immediately before and immediately after that task's edits, with an identical result): 67,980 B, 2,030 B over baseline_bytes. This overage PRE-DATES and is UNTOUCHED by that removal -- none of its editable files (verified live against measure-eager-context.sh's own per-file listing) are eager-loaded, so the removal could not move this figure in either direction. 2026-10-01: closed by a deliberate duplication trim across the predicted .claude/CLAUDE.md assembly's merge-sources/claudemd.md (the /orchestrate Command Reference row, the Multi-task syntax paragraph, and the Model Enforcement paragraph collapsed to short behavioural summaries plus existing/added pointers) and the eager rule agent-system/extensions/core/rules/git-workflow.md (two destructive-git narrative paragraphs relocated verbatim into context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md, which is not eager-loaded) -- landing at 65,402 B, 548 B under baseline_bytes. baseline_bytes remains unmoved; every relocated clause was verified present in its new non-eager home before the eager copy was cut. 2026-10-03: the consent-gated-push enforcement task's rule narrowing (rules/pr-prohibition.md's scoped /please exception, rules/git-workflow.md's enforcement pointer, and merge-sources/claudemd.md's new /please row) initially landed at 67,951 B, 2,001 B over baseline_bytes. Closed by trimming all three additions to compact pointer form (full detail relocated to context/standards/git-safety.md's "Consent-Gated Push and Destructive-Action Grants" section and context/standards/push-consent-relay.md, neither eager-loaded) -- landing at 65,927 B, 23 B under baseline_bytes. baseline_bytes remains unmoved. 2026-10-08: the record-versioning rule taxonomy and pattern library task's additions (rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md, 3,095 B eager, plus a merge-sources/claudemd.md Rules References bullet) measured 69,179 B, 3,229 B over baseline_bytes. Closed by relocating the Hard Mode section's full H2-H9 technique list, "when to use" criteria, and cost/composability detail from merge-sources/claudemd.md into context/guides/hard-mode-routing.md (verified present there before the eager copy was cut), the Syncprotect paragraph's full detail from merge-sources/claudemd.md into context/guides/loader-reference.md, the Never-Run over-staging bullets' full per-form rationale from rules/git-workflow.md into context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md, and rules/artifact-formats.md's Unified Sequential Numbering and Versioning worked examples into the new context/reference/artifact-numbering-and-versioning.md -- landing at 65,941 B, 9 B under baseline_bytes. baseline_bytes remains unmoved; every relocated clause was verified present in its new non-eager home before the eager copy was cut. 2026-10-09: the owner-labeled /approve command task added the FIRST entirely new extension (not bloat creep in an existing file) since this baseline's history began -- a new command needs a new claudemd-merged EXTENSION.md section for discoverability (matching every other command-providing extension's own convention; omitting it was rejected as a worse outcome than a documented baseline move, since it would make /approve undiscoverable through the normal Commands/Skill-Agent-Mapping documentation path every other extension uses). EXTENSION.md was compressed to a 105 B structural floor (one heading plus one clause plus a README.md pointer -- shorter than any other extension's own entry) before conceding the gap: this is strictly a FOR THIS reason the standing precedent of 'always trim, never bump' does not apply unmodified -- every prior overage was redistributable bloat in content this repository already carried, where a relocate-to-non-eager trim recovers real slack; this overage has no such slack to redistribute, since it is the floor cost of a capability that did not exist before. Landed at 66,045 B, 95 B over the prior 65,950 B baseline with the existing ~9 B margin already exhausted by the 2026-10-08 entry above (this task's own margin for error was effectively zero before any of its own content landed). Reviewed, dated baseline move, modest and non-generous per this field's own established tightness: 66,045 B rounded up to the next 100 B = 66,100 B. The two per-file ceiling_bytes entries above remain unmoved; this move is scoped to eager_load.baseline_bytes only. 2026-10-16: two independent eager additions landed since the prior measurement -- the foreign stash-pop guard's rule documentation (rules/git-workflow.md's 'Not blocked' paragraph narrowing 'permitted' to a session-identity distinction, plus its own Enforcement paragraph) and a self-referential exemption marker pair (rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md's version-ok:begin/end wrapping around the rule's own forbidden-vocabulary listing, required by the marker convention so the rule's self-description is not flagged by its own lint). Measured 67,088 B, 988 B over baseline_bytes. The marker-pair addition is a fixed floor cost of the exemption mechanism itself and has no further slack to redistribute. The stash-pop addition had real redistributable duplication: its Enforcement paragraph restated detail already carried in full in context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md's wrong-identity paragraph, and its 'Not blocked' paragraph repeated the FOREIGN-entry condition across two sentences. Both were tightened to the file's own existing compact 'Enforcement: ... Detail: <pointer>' style (matching the sibling No-History-Rewrites subsection two headings below it), recovering 381 B with no detail loss -- every fact in the trimmed text remains stated once, either inline or via the existing narrative-file pointer. Landed at 66,707 B, still 607 B over the prior baseline; this residual is the genuine, non-redistributable cost of two real safety-mechanism documentation additions (a FOREIGN-stash-pop data-loss guard and a lint self-exemption marker), not restatable bloat. Reviewed, dated baseline move, same rounding convention: 66,707 B rounded up to the next 100 B = 66,800 B. The two per-file ceiling_bytes entries above remain unmoved; this move is scoped to eager_load.baseline_bytes only. 2026-10-18: the standing 93 B margin left no durable headroom -- any ordinary eager addition would re-fire the gate. Route (a) resolution: a relocation trim, no further baseline movement. Audited the full eager set against its non-eager companions and found two genuine relocate-and-cut candidates, both verified present at their destination before the eager copy was cut: rules/artifact-formats.md's Phase Status Markers section, already fully stated in context/standards/status-markers.md's Plan-level vs. phase-level markers subsection (357 B recovered); and memory/EXTENSION.md's /distill command table (11 rows) plus its Memory Lifecycle ASCII diagram, already fully stated in context/project/memory/distill-usage.md's Quick Reference, Sub-Mode Workflows, and own Memory Lifecycle diagram (1,038 B recovered). Every other eager file re-examined (core merge-sources/claudemd.md's Task Management/Command Reference/Skill-to-Agent Mapping/Rules References sections, rules/git-workflow.md, rules/state-management.md, rules/pr-prohibition.md, email/EXTENSION.md) was found to already be single-stated quick-reference content at its established floor from prior trim rounds, not accidental duplication, so none of it was touched. Landed at 65,312 B, 1,488 B of headroom under baseline_bytes -- enough to absorb an ordinary eager addition without immediately re-firing the gate. baseline_bytes and both per-file ceiling_bytes entries remain unmoved; this move is scoped to eager_load.measured_bytes/measured_at and this note only. Both per-file ceiling margins noted above (commands/orchestrate.md 21,000 B ceiling with a razor-thin margin, skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md 24,000 B ceiling likewise razor-thin) are untouched by this entry and remain open follow-up candidates in the same noise class as this one, under ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE=hard. 2026-11-10: route (b) resolution -- a reviewed, dated baseline move, not a trim. A full audit of the growth since the 2026-10-18 entry traced it to six specific files: the sapience extension's entirely new EXTENSION.md (+2,065 B, the floor cost of a brand-new extension's own claudemd-merged section, matching the 2026-10-09 /approve-extension precedent exactly), core's merge-sources/claudemd.md (+734 B of genuinely new command rows and a changed-mechanism rewrite, not restatable detail), lean's EXTENSION.md (+387 B of bare pointer bullets), and small stale-reference corrections in literature/memory/nix. None of the six carried verbatim-duplicated content with a non-eager home to relocate to, so no route (a) trim applies here. Landed at 68,606 B, 1,806 B over the prior 66,800 B baseline. Reviewed, dated baseline move, same rounding convention: 68,606 B rounded up to the next 100 B = 68,700 B, leaving a thin 94 B margin -- the same razor-thin-margin pattern this field's own history already shows recurring (the 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-16 entries each left comparably little headroom), and this gate is expected to re-fire on the next ordinary eager addition by design, not as a surprise. The two per-file ceiling_bytes entries above remain unmoved; this move is scoped to eager_load.baseline_bytes (plus measured_bytes/measured_at) only.
